newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin says government reshuffle within days.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin says government reshuffle within days.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Thursday he would reshuffle his government in the next few days but gave no immediate details.

"There will definitely be changes...There will be a series of changes in the coming days," he told a news conference following a cabinet meeting. Earlier in the day, President Boris Yeltsin told parliament he wanted a government shake-up to end the deplorable economic and social situation in the country.
Chernomyrdin seemed at pains not to name names at the news conference but said he would announce his plan "literally" in the next few days.
"The issue is not about names...Tasks should determine the structure of the government and the personnel in the government," he said.
Chernomyrdin, who has been prime minister since December 1992, said he accepted Yeltsin's criticisms of the administration and would work to put matters right.

Kremlin sources say presidential chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais, a leading liberal, is likely to join the government with a powerful mandate over economic reform. Interfax news agency said on Thursday Yeltsin would sign a decree appointing Chubais first deputy prime minister on Friday.
